_comment: Ochorus glossary — archaic and theological terms found in the library's classics. Entries take precedence over the generic dictionary. Keys are lowercase; keep definitions to one plain-English sentence.
thou: You (singular subject) — the old familiar form of address.
thee: You (singular object): 'I tell thee' = 'I tell you'.
thine: Yours; also 'your' before a vowel ('thine eyes').
wrought: Worked; brought about or shaped: 'God wrought in them' = 'God worked in them'.
abide: To remain, stay, or dwell — in John 15, to live in continual union with Christ.
importunate: Persistently, even shamelessly urgent in asking (Luke 11:8).
importunity: Shameless persistence in asking — commended by Jesus as a mark of prevailing prayer.
succour: Help given in time of need.
manifold: Many and varied: 'the manifold grace of God'.
upbraid: To scold or reproach: God gives 'and upbraideth not' (James 1:5).
quicken: To make alive; to give life: 'quickened by the Spirit'.
countenance: The face, especially as it shows one's spirit: 'the Lord lift up His countenance upon you'.
bosom: The chest; figuratively, the place of closest intimacy ('in the Father's bosom').
girded: Belted up and ready — long robes were 'girded' for work or travel.
husbandman: A farmer; the one who tends a vineyard (John 15:1).
threshing: Beating grain to separate it from the husks.
winepress: The vat where grapes were trodden to press out the juice.
manna: The bread God provided daily in the wilderness (Exodus 16) — a picture of daily dependence.
leaven: Yeast; in Scripture usually a picture of hidden, spreading influence.
firstfruits: The first portion of the harvest, given to God as a pledge of the whole.
betoken: To signify; be a sign of.
covenant: A solemn, binding commitment between God and His people — stronger than a contract; God binds Himself by promise.
atonement: The reconciling work by which sin is dealt with and sinners are made 'at one' with God through Christ's death.
propitiation: Christ's sacrifice as that which satisfies God's righteous judgment against sin, turning wrath into favour (1 John 2:2).
expiation: The removal or covering of guilt by sacrifice.
justification: God's declaration that a believing sinner is righteous in His sight, on the ground of Christ's work — not earned, but given.
sanctification: The ongoing work of God making a believer actually holy in life and character.
regeneration: The new birth: God's Spirit imparting new spiritual life to a person (John 3).
consecration: Setting oneself, or being set, wholly apart for God.
intercession: Prayer on behalf of others; Christ 'ever lives to make intercession' for His people (Hebrews 7:25).
mediator: One who stands between two parties to reconcile them — 'one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus' (1 Timothy 2:5).
providence: God's continual care and government of all things, working them toward His good purposes.
omniscience: God's attribute of knowing all things.
immutable: Unchangeable — said of God and His promises.
ineffable: Too great to be expressed in words.
effectual: Actually producing its intended effect: 'the effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man' (James 5:16).
efficacious: Effective; actually accomplishing what it intends.
election: God's sovereign choice of His people in Christ before the foundation of the world (Ephesians 1:4).
predestination: God's determining beforehand the destiny of His people, unto adoption as sons (Ephesians 1:5).
adoption: God's act of receiving believers as His own children, with a child's standing and inheritance.
imputation: The reckoning of one person's standing to another: our sin reckoned to Christ, His righteousness reckoned to us.
imputed: Reckoned or credited to one's account.
carnal: Belonging to the flesh — governed by the old self-life rather than the Spirit.
mortify: To put to death — 'mortify the deeds of the body' (Romans 8:13) means to put sin to death, not merely restrain it.
mortification: The believer's putting sin to death by the Spirit.
perdition: Utter ruin; final loss and destruction.
chastening: God's fatherly discipline, painful for the moment but meant for our good (Hebrews 12:6).
chasteneth: Disciplines: 'whom the Lord loveth He chasteneth'.
longsuffering: Patient endurance of wrong or provocation without retaliation — an attribute of God.
meekness: Strength under control; a lowly gentleness that does not insist on itself — not weakness.
lowliness: Humility of mind; thinking of oneself rightly and little.
contrite: Crushed with godly sorrow for sin: 'a broken and a contrite heart' (Psalm 51:17).
penitent: Truly sorry for sin and turning from it.
temperance: Self-control (the older English word for it).
edification: Spiritual building up of a person or the church.
abasement: The state of being humbled or brought low.
begotten: Fathered; 'only begotten Son' translates a term meaning unique, one-of-a-kind Son.
sabbath: The appointed day of rest — a picture of resting in God's finished work.
tabernacle: The tent of God's dwelling among Israel; figuratively, God dwelling with His people.
mercy-seat: The gold cover of the ark where atoning blood was sprinkled — the meeting place of God and sinners (Exodus 25:22).
circumcision: The covenant sign given to Abraham; in the New Testament, a picture of the heart set apart to God.
uncircumcision: The state of being outside the covenant sign — Paul's shorthand for the Gentiles.
pharisee: A member of the strict religious party of Jesus' day, scrupulous about the law's letter.
publican: A tax collector for Rome — despised as a traitor and extortioner, yet welcomed by Jesus.
